name: Mississippi

agency.name: Mississippi State Oil and Gas Board

form.name: Application for Permit to Drill, Workover, Unit Reformation, Conversion or Change of Operator
form.notes: Read both pages. One form covers new drills and re-entries, workovers (recompletion, dual, commingle, horizontal deviation), unit reformation, conversion and change of operator. Fee $600 to drill, convert, or workover to dual or horizontal; $100 to recomplete another zone or change operator; proof of financial responsibility; certified plat; for new drills a reserve pit diagram, mud disposal statement and surface casing and cementing program. Latitude and longitude (NAD83, five decimals) for surface and bottom hole. Permit lapses after 12 months (6 for recompletions) if work not begun. Submitter e-mail, address and phone are on the form but not published as data.

api_number.n: API14 and API10 (well list); API (shapefile); form has an API No. box (assigned or existing)

permit_number.n: 'Permit #' in the Permit Search report (its JSON service and Excel export); also in the Permit Activity PDFs

lease_name.n: Form 2 has well name and number, field and reservoir, but no lease or unit name box

operator_name.n: EntityName on every permit in the Permit Search; Oper and OriginalOperator in the well list

operator_id.n: Form 2 asks the company name only, no operator number; registration Form 1 not read

operator_type.n: No business-type box on Form 2; registration Form 1 not read

bond.n: Proof of financial responsibility must accompany the Form 2 (Rules 4 and 63)

county.n: CountyName in the Permit Search; County (well list); CountyName (shapefile); county box on form

district.n: Only a 'field inspector information' box (office use); no district column in the data

field_pool.n: Field and PoolName (well list, pool filled on 12,090 of 35,218 wells); wildcat yes/no box on form

surface_latlon.n: Lat(NAD83), Long(NAD83) on 25,558 of 35,218 wells; form requires NAD83 decimal degrees

surface_plss.n: Sec, Twn, TwnDir, Rng, RngDir; form asks section, township, range and a location description

bottom_hole_loc.n: BH_Lat and BH_Long, only 598 of 35,218 wells; form asks BHL for directional or horizontal wells

lateral_path.n: Form asks only the bottom-hole point; no survey or path

elevation.n: Ground elevation (GR) box on Form 2; no elevation column in the files seen

surface_owner.n: Not asked; the ownership question on the form is about the drilling unit, not the surface

well_type.n: Type (OIL, GAS, SWD, EOR, DH...) in the well list is the well's type today, not at permit time; form has the boxes

work_type.n: 'Permit Types' in the Permit Search: OPD original, OPI injection, workover, conversion and change-of-operator codes

proposed_depth_md.n: 'Permit Depth' in the Permit Search and Permit Activity PDFs (MD or TVD not stated); form asks proposed or actual MD

proposed_depth_tvd.n: TVD box (proposed or actual); well list TotalVerticalDepth_TVD filled on only 528 wells, meaning not labeled

target_formation.n: PoolName (pool, not necessarily the target); form asks field and reservoir

casing_program.n: Proposed surface casing and cementing program attached (new drills); length of surface casing box

cement_program.n: Cementing program attached with the casing program (new drills)

pressure_control.n: No BOP item on Form 2 or its instructions

pit_waste.n: Reserve pit diagram and statement of mud disposal method attached (new drills)

fracture_plan.n: Not asked on Form 2 (a link to a chemical disclosure registry is on the home page)

frac_dates.n: Rule 1.26 and Form 3 ask for no fracture dates; only a 48-hour notice goes to the field inspector

frac_chemicals.n: Form 3 must list chemicals with CAS numbers, or state they went to FracFocus; no published list seen

frac_additives.n: Form 3 asks each additive's type, trade name and supplier (Rule 1.26); no published list seen

frac_amounts.n: Form 3 asks volumes in gallons or pounds and maximum percent by mass; no published figures seen

spacing_unit.n: Acres ('SIZE') in Permit Activity PDFs; form has drilling-unit acres, distance to unit line, docket and order boxes

spacing_exception.n: Instructions: exceptions to statewide rules need a petition to the Board; docket and order number boxes

mineral_owner.n: Yes/no statement on separately owned tracts and agreement to develop (state code 53-3-7); no owner names

fee.n: $600 to drill, convert or workover to dual or horizontal; $100 recomplete or change operator

notice_hearing.n: Docket and order boxes when a Board petition is needed; no notice step on the form

date_received.n: Date box next to the submitter; not in the bulk files

date_approved.n: 'Date Approved' in the Permit Search, every permit since 2019 in one request; the shapefile's PermitDate runs under it

date_expires.n: No date box; instructions say it lapses after 12 months (6 for recompletions) if work not begun

spud_date.n: Form gives only the approximate start date; Well Date List has an 'Event' filter whose options were not seen

completion_date.n: Completion is on Form 3; Well Date List 'Event' options were not seen

status.n: Status and Active (well list); status description in shapefile; includes expired and cancelled permits

plat_image.n: Certified plat to scale attached; not seen online

form_image.n: Permit Activity PDFs are lists, not the form; online document access not checked

completion_report.n: Form 3 is the completion report per Form 2 text; online access not checked

logs.n: Home page menu shows 'Scout Card & Log Search'; not opened

production_link.n: Downloads page lists a daily production CSV (16.6 MB); columns not read

sources.name: Well shape files with additional fields (wells_otherfields, ESRI shapefile in a zip, daily)
activity_types: permit to drill, by current well type (oil, gas, dry hole, injection, brine disposal, gas storage, monitor...)
sources.tested: One GET of the 2026-10-31 zip: 200, 1.4 MB, holds .dbf, .shp, .shx, .prj. DBF has 25,281 records and 13 attributes; PermitDate is a date field (earliest 1905-11-01, six records are 00000000, newest 2026-10-21). Permit dates per year: 2023 48, 2024 22, 2025 29, 2026 18 (to Oct 21), against the Board's own totals of 67, 50, 37 and 20 (to August). It holds only located wells and lacks expired and cancelled permits, so its counts run 22 to 56 percent under the Board's: not used. The file names carry the day and the listing page keeps about a week of them.

sources.name: Well info list, all wells (CSV, daily)
activity_types: all wells with current type and status; permit-stage statuses (expired, cancelled, permitted) are included
sources.tested: One GET of the 2026-10-30 file: 200, 12.8 MB, header row of 30 columns, 35,218 wells, no date column of any kind. Type values include OIL, GAS, DH, SWD, EOR, EX (expired location); Status values include EX (expired permit) 3,298 and CA (permit cancelled) 329; WellSlant Vertical, Directional or Horizontal; latitude on 25,558 wells. The Downloads page names the newest file of the last four days. The producer reads API10 and Type only, to give an original permit's well its type.

sources.name: MSOGB Permit Search report (one row per permit the Board approves; filters by operator, field, county, permit type and date approved; its table is filled by the page's own script service)
activity_types: original permits to drill (OPD) and injection permits (OPI)
commingled, dual and triple completions (OPDC, OPDD, OPDT), conversions (CIP, CPI), workovers (WOP, WOPH, WOI, WOIH)
sources.tested: Read 2026-11-01. The page's table is filled by its own script, which POSTs the page's query (base64, field QueryToExcute) to /ajaxloadPDO.php and gets DataTables JSON back. One request for a date range with no other filter returns every permit since 2019-01-01 (5,540 rows, 2.5 MB, 7.6 s), identical row for row to the union of eight per-year requests. The Board's own permit-type list (RefCodes) gives the codes above. The first research's plain POST of the form returned only the header row, because the query is built by script. Page text says an export to Excel needs fewer than 3,500 rows. No documented interface: a redesign of the page would break a script.

sources.name: Permits to Drill, annual PDFs of counts by county and month (1987 to 2026)
activity_types: permits to drill (all well types together)
sources.tested: Folder listing (200, 40 yearly files 1987 to 2026) and the 2026 file: 200, 66 KB, text PDF. Counties by month; total row Jan to Aug 2026 is 2, 1, 1, 2, 5, 3, 3, 3 (20); the chart caption says Total 2025 = 37, Total 2026 = 20. The sheets for 2023 and later are text; 2022 and older are scans. The sheet counts new and injection permits to drill only and is updated by hand about two months late. The producer reads the two newest sheets on every run as its independent check.

sources.name: Permit Activity reports (PDF, one per board period, 2009 to 2026)
columns: unit size in acres and county
activity_types: permits to drill (OPD series seen); other series not seen
sources.tested: Tree listing (HTTP 200, 864 links, yearly folders from 2009) and one 2-page file: HTTP 200, 98 KB, text PDF with three permits, no header row, labels are not given for the date. The file named for 2026-10-20 was made in March 2026 and holds permits dated Oct 2025 to Jan 2026, and the listing has names dated after today, so file names do not date the content.

sources.name: MSOGB Online mapping and reporting (data mining application)
sources.tested: Not requested. The well list's DirectURL column points each well to this application's details page; its contents were not seen.

grade_reason: The Board's Permit Search report has one row per permit it approves (original permits to drill, injection, workovers, conversions, changes of operator) with Date Approved, permit number, permit type, operator, county and depth, and one request returns every permit since 2019. Held to B, not A: the report is a page's own script service with no documented interface; the well type comes from a separate daily well list and is the well's type today; there is no spud date. The daily shapefile is no substitute: it counts only located wells (59, 48, 22 and 29 for 2022 to 2025 against the Board's 88, 67, 50 and 37). Updated 2026-11-01: a producer reads the report each week and its new plus injection permits are within two of the Board's own yearly totals (119, 34, 60, 90, 66, 50, 37 for 2019 to 2025 against 119, 35, 61, 88, 67, 50, 37) and equal month by month for 2024 to 2026.
producer_plan: Built: d11_nat_ms.py. One POST to the Permit Search page's own service /ajaxloadPDO.php with the query the page builds for a date range (six columns: approval day, permit number, well number, operator, county, permit type; every permit since 2019-01-01, about 5,500 rows, 2.5 MB). The Board's well list CSV (Downloads page, newest of the last four days) gives the well's type by API10 for original permits, in memory. Bands from the Board's permit-type codes: OPD of an oil, gas, dry or test well = new; OPI, or an OPD for a service well = inj; commingled, dual and triple completions, conversions and workovers = rework; changes of operator = amend (one permit per well); H2S, PIT and unknown codes = other; redrill is null (the codes do not separate a re-entry from a new drill). Fluid from the well list's type (OIL, GAS; the rest unknown). Each run reads the Board's two newest yearly Permits to Drill PDFs (pdftotext) and refuses to write when new plus inj, less monitor wells, differs from the sheet's total by more than 3 permits or 8 percent. Six requests 3 s apart, about 27 s; a month counts as complete 14 days after it ends.
privacy_notes: The Permit Search and the well list name company operators (no phone, e-mail or street address columns); the producer names an operator only if it is a corporation, LLC or partnership. The Permit Activity PDFs carry a contractor field. The blank form asks for a submitter's e-mail, address and phone, which are not in the open data.
